title: RBAC: add permissions and default roles for SIEM audit export management
author: Kaitlyn Nguyen
description:
Implements least-privilege RBAC permissions/scopes for the SIEM-ready audit export beta. This PR introduces explicit permissions for (a) managing audit export configurations (create/update/delete/enable/disable), (b) rotating/attaching destination credentials, and (c) viewing exporter delivery health/status (lag, last success, last error) in Console and via API. Permissions are wired through the control-plane authz layer and included in default enterprise roles with feature-flag gating. Linked: ENG-5173.

Motivation: We need to allow Security/Compliance and Workspace Admins to manage export destinations without granting broad platform-admin access, while ensuring auditors/support can view delivery health without being able to exfiltrate secrets or modify destinations.

Scope:
- New permission names + descriptions in the RBAC registry
- Policy checks in the control-plane endpoints for export config CRUD and status
- Default role mappings for "Workspace Admin", "Security Admin", and "Auditor" (beta)
- Explicit denial of secret material access via status endpoints (status returns credential_ref metadata only)

Non-scope:
- Fine-grained per-destination egress allowlist policy (separate PR in exporter)
- UI changes (Console will consume the status endpoint + permission-gated actions)

Rollout:
- Permission checks are enabled regardless, but routes are still gated behind the SIEM export feature flag + tenant allowlist (ENG-5184).

Test plan:
- Added unit tests for permission evaluation and role mapping
- Added request tests for export config endpoints returning 403 for insufficient perms
- Manual: verified Admin can create config; Auditor can view status but cannot edit/rotate creds

Security notes:
- Status endpoint returns only redacted error messages (no headers/tokens) and a credential reference ID, not secret values.
- "Rotate credentials" is its own permission to avoid accidental broad write access.

Docs:
- Internal permission catalog updated (follow-up for external admin docs tracked in PM-858).

notable_snippet:
New permissions (names are final per Security review):
- audit_export.manage
  - Allows create/update/delete/enable/disable of export configs and filters.
- audit_export.rotate_credentials
  - Allows updating credential references / initiating credential rotation flows.
- audit_export.view_status
  - Allows reading exporter status (lag/health/last_success/last_error_redacted) for configured exports.

Important: audit_export.view_status does NOT allow reading destination configuration details beyond destination type + redacted identifiers; config read is included under audit_export.manage to keep status access safe for Auditor role.
review_conversation:
Ethan Park (review, 2025-03-27): Can we separate "config read" from "config write"? I’d like Auditor to see the list of destinations, but not edit.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Agree. In this PR I kept config read under manage to reduce surface area during beta. If we want split semantics, I can add audit_export.view_config in a follow-up; it will require API changes because handlers currently share the same read path used by the UI edit page.
Ethan Park: OK for beta. Please add a TODO comment and track it.

Marcus Lin (review, 2025-03-28): Please confirm that error messages coming back via status endpoint cannot include tokens/headers/URLs with query params.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Added redaction in the status response mapping to strip headers and query strings; also capped length to 1KB and added allowlist of error codes. Added tests to ensure tokens are not present.

Kevin Osei (review, 2025-03-29): Permission naming: I prefer audit_export.manage over audit_export.write for clarity. Also, rotate creds must be distinct.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Updated names accordingly and regenerated the permission catalog.

Chloe Martin (review, 2025-04-01): Console expects 403 vs 404 for insufficient privileges so it can show "Request access" CTA. Are we consistent across endpoints?
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Yes—middleware now returns 403 with error code AUTHZ_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and includes required_permissions list (no resource details).

Diego Santos (review, 2025-04-02): For Dedicated, do we need any deployment-mode specific scoping? E.g. org-level vs workspace-level.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Permissions are workspace-scoped; org-level behavior remains unchanged. Dedicated uses the same workspace boundary in control plane.
